title: Evaluating the Effectiveness of BEX-EDS SEM for Rapid Forensic Sand Analysis
content: Sand is a ubiquitous material found in diverse environments, making it a valuable forensic trace evidence tool for determining geographic origin [1]. Traditional forensic soil analysis relies on optical microscopy for color and textural analysis, bulk geochemical characterization, and mineralogical identification [1, 2]. These methods can be time-intensive and often cannot resolve fine-scale compositional and morphological variations necessary for precise forensic discrimination. In contrast, scanning electron microscopy (SEM) enables higher-resolution imaging of grain morphology, as well as detailed elemental and mineralogical characterization. In this study, we explore a novel advanced forensic methodology by applying SEM equipped with energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS) and backscatter electron X-ray (BEX) detection followed by precise mineral and particle feature analysis to rapidly characterize sand samples from distinct geographic locations across the United States. Samples were selected from coastal and inland sites across the United States, including Mashpee, MA; West Haven, CT; Key West, FL; San Francisco, CA; San Diego, CA; and Chicago, IL, to encompass a range of sedimentary sources and transport histories.
